findings.rule: CLAUDE.md, "Watch out for": "**Role values are in transition.** The database holds `admin` / `member`; the specs target `admin | manager | user | viewer`. New authorization code must handle both"
findings.claim: the request detail page casts the raw session role instead of normalizing it, so every capability read on this new screen is made against a value the capability matrix does not contain when the database holds the legacy `member`

witness.detail: `const role = session.role as Role` at line 46. `session.role` is typed `string` and carries `Membership.role` verbatim. `can()` is a bare table lookup with a false fallback (`CAPABILITY_MATRIX[role]?.[capability] ?? false`, packages/validation/src/index.ts:716-718), so `CAPABILITY_MATRIX['member']` is undefined and every capability silently reads false instead of being mapped to `user`. The two sibling files written in the same task normalize first and say why: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:93 `const role: Role = normalizeRole(session.role)` and apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx:41. The server does the same, once, in requireCaller (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:861). The cast also asserts a falsehood to the type system: `Role` is 'admin'|'manager'|'user'|'viewer' and the value may be 'member'.

findings.suggestedFix: `const role: Role = normalizeRole(session.role);`, matching page.tsx:93. Today the only capability read here is `view-all-requests`, which both `user` and `member` lack, so the wrong answer and the right answer coincide — that coincidence is what makes this a trap for the next capability added to the screen rather than a visible bug now.

CLAUDE.md, Testing: "Selectors are `data-testid` only, and the ids are named in the specs."
findings.claim: requirement 36 was rewritten by this diff to demand a reassign banner and control on the list row, but requirement 45 enumerates the row's contents exhaustively without them and the Required data-testid list names no id for either, so no implementation can satisfy both rules

witness.detail: This diff changed requirement 36 from "appears under the reassignment filter" to "draws the reassign banner and the reassign control on the row and the detail screen". The detail screen honours it (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/[requestId]/page.tsx:273 renders request-detail-assignee-inactive-banner, :328 renders request-detail-reassign-btn). RequestRow.tsx contains no occurrence of `assignee.inactive` — its only `inactive` strings are Badge tone values at :10 and :127 — although the field is on the row data (types.ts:61). To implement it an agent must both contradict requirement 45's enumeration and invent two data-testids the spec's Required data-testid section does not name, which CLAUDE.md and .claude/agents/implementer.md:93 both forbid. A third statement disagrees with requirement 36 as well: specs/requests/README.md:84 still reads "flagged `assigneeInactive` and surface in the reassignment filter", a filter requirement 36 now says does not exist and that the closed filter set cannot express.

findings.suggestedFix: A human decides one of two: narrow requirement 36 back to the detail screen (and correct README.md:84), or extend requirement 45 and the Required data-testid list with the row-level ids and give the behaviour a test case. Either way README.md:84 needs the same correction.

findings.claim: the banner this diff adds promises "thirteen of them ... the list is exhaustive so it can be checked", and at least five statements that requests/01 overrules carry no amendment mark and now assert the opposite of what ships

This is the second pass on the same defect: the previous run's carried blocker F1 named nine unmarked statements, thirteen were then marked, and five remain. findings.rule: CLAUDE.md, Design system: "Anything missing goes *into* the design system and is recorded in that spec's \"DS gaps\" table, never improvised per screen." Restated by specs/requests/01-requests.md:695.
findings.claim: three components improvise native textarea and date controls because @ds ships neither, and their comments assert the gap is "recorded in the spec's DS-gaps table" — the spec contains no such table

witness.detail: `grep -rn "DS gap\|DS-gaps" specs/requests/` returns exactly one line, 01-requests.md:695, which is the sentence stating the obligation. No table exists in the spec or in specs/requests/README.md. The code asserts otherwise in three places: NewRequestModal.tsx:79 "Both are recorded in the spec's DS-gaps table", :316-317 "@ds ships no textarea ... Recorded in the spec's DS gaps", :405 "@ds ships no date field either — same precedent, same DS-gaps row". Two further screens improvise the same way: DeclineRequestModal.tsx:126-161 (the textarea, verified) and [requestId]/page.tsx:364-396. findings.rule: .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md, sweep 9 Boundary sweep: "Enumerate every pair that must agree across a file boundary: ... a documented value and the code that reads it. ... **Blocks when** they do not."
findings.claim: `--no-carry` is documented in ship.mjs's header and usage string and is read by wf.mjs, but ship.mjs never forwards it, so the flag silently does the opposite of what it says

witness.detail: Run `node scripts/ship.mjs specs/requests/01-requests.md --no-carry` in a tree holding an earlier non-`ready` run of that spec with code blockers. ship.mjs:387-392 builds the init call from `opt('from')` and `opt('carry')` only; `--no-carry` appears in ship.mjs at just two places, the usage comment at :25 and the usage string at :384, and is read nowhere. wf.mjs:393 therefore never sees `args['no-carry']`, falls through to `findCarrySource(specRel)` at :395, and the run initialises with carriedFindings populated — the exact opposite of the documented "start clean, inheriting nothing". This run is the proof the path is live: run.json carries carriedFrom "2026-09-01T14-44-29_requests-01-requests#review" and two carried findings, both found automatically.

findings.suggestedFix: `...(flag('no-carry') ? ['--no-carry'] : [])` alongside the `--carry` spread at :390. Everything else in the carry mechanism checks out: carried findings reach pre_implement and implement only, are spent once, and no gate is weakened.

findings.rule: CLAUDE.md, Implementing specs: "**Agent prompts are rules only.** A definition under `.claude/agents/` states the desired behaviour and the prohibitions" — and .claude/agents/implementer.md:22: "**Never edit anything under `specs/`.** The spec is the contract you are being checked against."
findings.claim: task T9 assigns a file under specs/ to the implementer, which the implementer's definition prohibits absolutely; the plan therefore directs an agent to break its own contract, and that is why the spec-10 bookkeeping has now failed twice

witness.detail: T9 is titled "Bookkeeping: keep user-management spec 10 telling the truth about the endpoint it used to own" and its files array is ["specs/user-management/10-organization-requests-page.md"]. .claude/agents/implementer.md:22 states "Never edit anything under `specs/`", and :159 states "`spec` is the only address you may use" — that is, the implementer's route for a spec defect is to raise a finding, not to edit the file. The edit nevertheless happened (git diff f06c7d84..HEAD -- specs/user-management/10-organization-requests-page.md is 109 lines), and it came back incomplete twice running: the previous run's carried blocker F1 named nine unmarked statements, this pass finds five still unmarked (F3). A spec change made as a side effect of an implementation task is the opposite of CLAUDE.md's "change the spec first, deliberately."

findings.suggestedFix: Drop T9 from the plan. A dependent spec that a shipping spec amends is a spec edit a person makes deliberately before the run, or a `spec` finding raised during it — not a task handed to an agent forbidden from touching specs/.

findings.claim: requirement 44 makes the sidebar badge issue an unfiltered GET .../requests from every page for every signed-in member, and for an admin or manager that call still runs the whole spec-10 vacation aggregation — where before this spec only opening the Requests page triggered it

For a caller holding view-requests, listRequests:245 always attaches the vacation section, which runs findMany over all VacationRequests of the org with no take and no status predicate when status defaults to 'all', a second findMany over all VacationReserveTransactions for those memberships, and an O(members x requests) balance loop at :167-198. findings.suggestedFix: The badge needs only counts.waitingOnMe and vacation.pendingCount; a count-only path for a query-less call would avoid the aggregation. Decide it in the spec, not in the service.
